signals.summary: Customer stated that if he had the choice, he would change how the auto start-stop works. Customer commented that the…
signals.quote: Customer stated that if he had the choice, he would change how the auto start-stop works. Customer commented that the system does not feel as smooth as he would like when pulling away, and that he notices the way it turns off and back on. Writer explained that besides turning off the MSA for that drive, there is also an Auto H button located near the start-stop button that the customer should try the next time he is in the car. Writer went over the Auto H, or auto hold, function and described how, when the vehicle is brought to a stop, it will remain stopped even after the driver lifts their foot off the brake pedal, and will only move once the accelerator pedal is pressed. Writer gave the example of sitting at a red light and asked the customer to see whether the car stays stationary or begins to roll ahead when the brake pedal is released before pressing the accelerator. Writer instructed the customer to check for a green light on the Auto H button and stated that a quick press will switch the feature off. Writer clarified that this feature is very useful in stop-and-go traffic, drive-throughs and similar situations where the driver wants to take their foot off the brake while the vehicle remains stopped until the accelerator is used. Writer also noted that auto hold can sometimes lead to slightly jerky movements when parking and suggested this could be playing a role in the smoothness concern the customer mentioned.

Writer recommended the customer bring the vehicle to the dealership as soon as possible for diagnosis to find out what is causing the low range.

signals.quote: Customer reported the vehicle has inconsistent scheduled charging, with the car often ignoring the programmed 8:30 PM time slot. Customer noted that sometimes it begins charging immediately after being plugged in even though the settings are not set to charge right away, and at other times it will unexpectedly start charging around 5 PM or 4 PM despite being set for 8:30 PM. Customer stated the system will also change the charging configuration on its own, switching from the time slot setting to charge immediately without any action from the customer. Customer estimated this behavior occurs about half the time, with the other 50 percent working as intended. Customer indicated the issue happens whether charging from roughly 75 percent state of charge to a 90 percent target or at other battery levels, and that it was present both before and after a software update. Customer stated all charging is done at home using a 250 volt outlet in the garage. Customer mentioned the AC limit was originally at 48 amps but later reduced to 32 amps to be cautious, and the problem occurs at both limits. Customer added the outlet is capable of supporting up to 48 amps. Customer advised the vehicle was brought to the dealership, but technicians were unable to duplicate the problem even though the customer provided app screenshots showing the time slot at 8:30 PM while the car charged at 8 PM. Customer said the dealership performed tests and reached out to BMW engineers, but they were unable to resolve the issue. Customer stated the dealership did not reset the software or apply any fix, and engineers concluded there was nothing to be done. Writer suggested the customer continue to observe the charging behavior and contact the dealership again if the problem persists so they can try to reproduce and diagnose it.

signals.summary: it's a good car, but the way the map magnification is controlled on-screen is extremely dangerous and very distracting, and…
signals.quote: it's a good car, but the way the map magnification is controlled on-screen is extremely dangerous and very distracting, and could easily cause accidents just like using mobile phones. the old setup with a central control knob meant the driver could alter map zoom without taking attention off the road, whereas this new finger-on-screen method does exactly the opposite. i do have a simple workaround that would only need software changes, not a full redesign of the car: the knurled volume wheel could be used for both volume and map zoom, switching between them with a double click on the wheel. i cannot emphasise enough how strongly i feel about this; with this stupid system it is only a matter of time before someone gets killed.

signals.summary: the car is enjoyable to drive and uses less petrol than i expected. on the downside it is overcomplicated, with…
signals.quote: the car is enjoyable to drive and uses less petrol than i expected. on the downside it is overcomplicated, with far too much reliance on the display screen where proper physical buttons would be safer and more practical. there are two temperature sliders that stay permanently synced, which makes one of them pointless and irritating. there is also a software issue where the recommended tyre pressures keep changing, apparently because the tyre information is not stored correctly. the car was delivered without an owner's handbook; after getting one later, i find it very poor, with no clear way to see which parts apply to my specific car. it wastes space on general 'principle' sections instead of clearly explaining how features operate and how to control them. finally, the door mirrors stick out too far and add unnecessary width, they could definitely be smaller.

signals.summary: over roughly the last 15 years ive had a new 1 series each time, and every version has got better.…
signals.quote: over roughly the last 15 years ive had a new 1 series each time, and every version has got better. the 123 is the best yet, x drive has definitely improved the road holding and the petrol consumption is excellent. i feel the air conditioning controls should be manual, same for the sat nav. the wheel design needs changing as theyre a real nuisance to clean, just like the front grill. apart from that its a first class car and im already looking forward to my next bmw in around 2.5 years.

signals.summary: when i bought the car they said it came with a paper manual, and i even had to sign a…
signals.quote: when i bought the car they said it came with a paper manual, and i even had to sign a form saying the manual was with the vehicle, but there was none when it was delivered. i reported this straight away and was told one would be posted. nothing turned up. went past the showroom about a month later, went in, and was again told a manual would be sent. waited another month, still nothing, so i emailed the salesman who once more promised it would be sent, and again nothing. just tell me if you have stopped supplying hard copy manuals, dont keep putting me off hoping i wont remember.

signals.summary: this new car is easier to drive than my old manual one. i used to struggle stretching my legs to…
signals.quote: this new car is easier to drive than my old manual one. i used to struggle stretching my legs to reach the pedals, so not needing my left leg now really helps. it has lots of features that weren't on my last car, some of them are clever and useful. the orange triangle lights on the wing mirrors are very helpful and weren't there before. i also like the speed warning alerts. overall it's an upgrade from my previous car, i do like it and would recommend it to family and friends.

signals.summary: i would really have liked the option of a manual gearbox, and that would have pushed my rating higher, but…
signals.quote: i would really have liked the option of a manual gearbox, and that would have pushed my rating higher, but as with many brands it seems bmw no longer offers this to buyers. overall the car is great fun to drive when you are not manoeuvring. a few small niggles: still no intermittent setting for the windscreen wipers when they are not in auto mode; the driver seatbelt cannot be adjusted for height so i am always fiddling with it while driving; the driver seat could go lower to give extra headroom when getting in; software updates wipe out settings, especially autohold being turned on. before purchase i would have appreciated a brochure clearly listing the equipment on each model so i could compare, and when reading the handbook, to know whether my car is supposed to have a given feature. also, comfort access does not include foot boot opening even though it was shown in the app before delivery.

signals.summary: i haven't been happy with it because i couldn't get the options i wanted. the salesman told me bmw wouldn't…
signals.quote: i haven't been happy with it because i couldn't get the options i wanted. the salesman told me bmw wouldn't give a price or a delivery date, so i had to go without them. the sport seats don't have any lumbar support and i find them really uncomfortable, with my back starting to ache after only a few miles. when i did the test drive it was in a 2 series, and those seats had lumbar support, were comfortable, and i didn't get any back ache at all. this car also doesn't have any lashing straps, and the salesman said they only come if you add the luggage net option. in the details for that option it clearly says there are 3 additional lashing eyes, so i ordered the luggage net through the salesman and picked it up from the stores, but it turned up with no lashing eyes. i didn't buy it or pay for it online either. later i read an article saying all bmw 1 series 2025 models are supposed to have a lashing eye fitted as standard. on the plus side, the car itself drives really well, with no body roll and very good brakes, and it feels like a driver's car even as an auto. i still think it would be better as a manual.

signals.summary: i like driving my 120 m sport and it covers all my motoring needs. it is comfy, reliable, quiet and…
signals.quote: i like driving my 120 m sport and it covers all my motoring needs. it is comfy, reliable, quiet and enjoyable. the only irritating thing is there is no paper driver guide, so i have to waste time scrolling through the electronic manual.

signals.summary: really like the styling. solid performance and the fuel economy numbers are excellent. comfy, particularly for driver and front passenger.…
signals.quote: really like the styling. solid performance and the fuel economy numbers are excellent. comfy, particularly for driver and front passenger. the screen functions were confusing until i got used to them. quite unhappy there was no updated driver manual to help enjoy it straight away.

signals.summary: there is plenty to appreciate but also a couple of niggles. from behind the wheel the suspension feels quite firm,…
signals.quote: there is plenty to appreciate but also a couple of niggles. from behind the wheel the suspension feels quite firm, possibly just more noticeable because the cabin is so quiet. the software is very complex and the manual doesn't help much, particularly when i try to use it on my phone; a proper printed booklet might be better. the satnav has sent me down more single track lanes in the past 3 months than i've driven in the last 3 years, so i don't really trust it now. i do, however, like how it integrates with the guidance on the dash.

signals.summary: moved from a manual bmw to this automatic and it's very easy to drive. good mpg, great looking car, satnav…
signals.quote: moved from a manual bmw to this automatic and it's very easy to drive. good mpg, great looking car, satnav works well and the camera system is excellent.

signals.summary: the low rating is due to there being no manual option. the automatic gearbox doesnt feel smooth and tends to…
signals.quote: the low rating is due to there being no manual option. the automatic gearbox doesnt feel smooth and tends to hop between gears, especially when pulling off, which is quite disappointing. another downside is having to stretch forward to touch the information screen; the old navigation wheel setup was much safer when driving and wanting to adjust any settings.

signals.summary: i'm really delighted with my new bmw, it is a joy to drive. this is my first automatic after years…
signals.quote: i'm really delighted with my new bmw, it is a joy to drive. this is my first automatic after years of using manual cars and it definitely makes driving simpler and more comfortable. the auto gear changes are smooth and quiet, and the acceleration feels quick and effortless. i'm also a big fan of the automatic handbrake. the interior was a key factor in choosing this car and it has lived up to what i hoped for. the sat nav screen is easy to read and straightforward to operate, and i've had a lot of fun playing with all the different lighting options. everything feels sturdy and thought-through with the driver in mind, and i'm very pleased with the decision i made. our salesman daniel at rochdale made the whole buying process effortless and kept me well informed throughout.

signals.summary: overall the car looks great and the mild hybrid setup performs well. handling is generally very good, though it does…
signals.quote: overall the car looks great and the mild hybrid setup performs well. handling is generally very good, though it does hesitate when going over bigger cats eyes on the motorway. the app connection can be awkward and quite often fails entirely. the trip stats feature worked initially but then just stopped on 9th feb. the manual and the youtube guides do not give the right instructions for this new 120 model, so i have been forced to dig around myself to work out how to sort it, which is frustrating. visually, the radio station display is also a letdown.

signals.summary: idrive 9 is awful. feels bloated, with loads of stuff nobody needs. trying to use it while actually driving feels…
signals.quote: idrive 9 is awful. feels bloated, with loads of stuff nobody needs. trying to use it while actually driving feels unsafe. i really don't want to have a conversation with the car just to adjust the fan. the home screen can't be changed to anything useful. if this system stays like this, i won't buy another bmw. the car itself is very good, but id9 completely kills the fun of driving it.

signals.summary: the car itself is ok but the infotainment ruins the driving feel i was hoping for. you have dropped the…
signals.quote: the car itself is ok but the infotainment ruins the driving feel i was hoping for. you have dropped the basics in favour of stuff that does not matter like light colours and other trivia. before every drive i spend about 5 minutes setting everything how i want, and it still goes back to the default as soon as i stop. the endless stream of messages is distracting, same with the pings and bongs whenever the car does not like what i do. for a while i really thought i had a puncture until i found out it was the car shaking through the steering wheel. there is no need for most of this info and i think some of it is distracting and maybe even lethal. i want to watch the road, not the screen. and useful things like the petrol gauge are tiny and almost hidden on the display. out of space

signals.summary: good car to drive, it handles well and is quick enough for what i need. interior is nice, but the…
signals.quote: good car to drive, it handles well and is quick enough for what i need. interior is nice, but the touchscreen setup is frankly unsafe to use on the move and really needs an idrive wheel to be safer. i don't see why that was removed other than to cut costs. turning off the speed limit and the equally risky lane departure warning is too fiddly, there should be a button for each. the my modes feature in this 120 is almost useless, adding no real driving benefit, just extra complexity and probably cost. the boot is too small for a car of this size. even with these complaints, it still suits my needs perfectly right now, and despite the over-complex tech the interface is still far better than my wife's mercedes a class.

signals.summary: the car itself is amazing, but i find it a real issue that lots of basic functions (like the stop…
signals.quote: the car itself is amazing, but i find it a real issue that lots of basic functions (like the stop start function) are only reachable through the screen, which is very distracting when you're actualy driving.

signals.summary: overall it is a good car but i do have issues: drivetrain - it behaves more like a plain fwd…
signals.quote: overall it is a good car but i do have issues: drivetrain - it behaves more like a plain fwd than a rear-biased 4wd and you can feel torque steer. dashboard controls - getting rid of the physical buttons and burying everything in the touchscreen is awkward and could even be unsafe. the ui has become a nuisance: to switch into sport mode i have to go through several steps, and since the voice control is flaky and i don't want to chat to my car, that's not an option. when using nav i have to 1) hit the mode button on the centre console, 2) pick the mode on the display, then 3) tap nav on the side of the screen to get the map back. build quality - the plastics feel low grade and there are rattles, particularly around the dash. steering wheel - this is meant to be a sporty hatch, so please stop fitting wheels sized like they belong on a boat.

signals.summary: performance, comfort and sound system are good. the displays, especially the touchscreen for basic functions, really let the car down.…
signals.quote: performance, comfort and sound system are good. the displays, especially the touchscreen for basic functions, really let the car down. even once you know where things like the heating controls sit on the screen, the time spent glancing away from the windscreen and trying to hit the exact spot takes attention away from actually driving and focusing on the road!   this is my fourth 1 series bmw (first m) and although it is still early days, i will not be rushing to buy another.

signals.summary: it is a comfortable place to sit, even if it is not exactly glamorous. driving is mostly good. the sunroof…
signals.quote: it is a comfortable place to sit, even if it is not exactly glamorous. driving is mostly good. the sunroof is a let-down though, i would have preferred a larger one. the fact that you push forward for reverse and pull back for drive feels completely crazy to me, i dont understand why anyone would set it up like that. the display isnt great either, everything is tiny, and i only just noticed i was almost out of fuel because it is so hard to see the fuel level. i have almost finished setting up the heating and cooling, but working out where the air actually goes is awkward and there are loads of little controls to fiddle with. i absolutely hate the parking and reversing assist, the car is constantly yelling at me, with margins that seem far too wide. it keeps making warning sounds for no reason i can figure out, and the car has already cut out twice and then would not go either backwards or forwards. i am now about to take it in to be checked.

signals.summary: i really like how the car looks and the interior layout. the handling is excellent, but the suspension is very…
signals.quote: i really like how the car looks and the interior layout. the handling is excellent, but the suspension is very firm and not very comfortable. the touch screen is handy, but also quite complicated to use.

signals.summary: engine feels a bit underpowered. the rotating wheel on the center console is gone, so poking at lots of apps…
signals.quote: engine feels a bit underpowered. the rotating wheel on the center console is gone, so poking at lots of apps on one screen feels awkward and unsafe. also missing any all-wheel drive options.

signals.summary: initial impressions were really positive, but after a few weeks there were technical issues and it had to spend half…
signals.quote: initial impressions were really positive, but after a few weeks there were technical issues and it had to spend half a day at the service centre in norchester. it was fine again until this month, when a similar fault occurred: the main screen went completely black, making everything it controls unusable. i took it back to the service centre, where they kept it for the day and then overnight to carry out a full reset. they did good work there in norchester, to be fair. hopefully it is now sorted, but the whole situation has definitely taken the shine off the experience of getting and driving my new car.

signals.quote: i do like the car overall. however i find the instructions quite unclear, both within the app and on the car's display.

signals.summary: it is enjoyable to drive and very economical, but i do have concerns. getting rid of the idrive controller feels…
signals.quote: it is enjoyable to drive and very economical, but i do have concerns. getting rid of the idrive controller feels like going backwards, and having almost everything on the touch screen is distracting and not intuitive. i have had 9 bmws and this one is the hardest to configure, even for simple functions.

signals.summary: i'm not a fan of touch screens at all, and using them for heater controls is silly, especially when you…
signals.quote: i'm not a fan of touch screens at all, and using them for heater controls is silly, especially when you might need to adjust them while driving. physical, tactile switches are far better. the steering wheel is too thick, not that comfortable, and definitely not as good as on my earlier bmws.

signals.summary: I had a 118i m sport before and the 120 m sport has had all the useful bits stripped out…
signals.quote: I had a 118i m sport before and the 120 m sport has had all the useful bits stripped out and is not a sport model at all! this is our 6th bmw and easily the worst car we've ever had. 1. no 12v socket in the boot, a ridiculous penny pinching move. 2. no phone charging points in the back. 3. no climate controls in the rear. 4. no fog lights. 5. no leather seats. 6. no visible exhaust, sport model?? 7. basic 18" alloys (19" were standard on the 118i), sport model?? 8. thin, cheap carpets with poor grip and no m sport trim. every one of these came standard on the 118i m sport and the 120 m sport is marketed as its direct replacement! the 120 m sport is about £7/8k more, plus paying again for all the things removed, making it a pricey car and the worst thing ever to come out of a bmw showroom. total rubbish!

signals.summary: the size and the way it handles feel spot on, and its running performance is the best. it fits 5…
signals.quote: the size and the way it handles feel spot on, and its running performance is the best. it fits 5 people, and i think it is the best option as long as you are ok with the firm ride and not taking big luggage.

signals.summary: this car has been a total let down. if i could get my old 2021 m135i back i would be…
signals.quote: this car has been a total let down. if i could get my old 2021 m135i back i would be far happier. the apps and drive modes are overly complex, not user friendly at all, and far too distracting and difficult to use while driving, so you basically have to stop to deal with them. the way it handles is like a boat in a storm, no matter which drive setting you choose, and it is definitely not a sport hatch. the driving sound is too fake, the interior feels cheap, and a lot of practical conveniences have disappeared. there is no storage box on the driver side of the dash and no 12v socket in the boot. the m sport seats now lack support and comfort, unlike the previous standard version of those seats. after 3 months in this i am already looking to swap to another car. it is the worst car change i have made, not an improvement at all, and a big regrettable mistake.

signals.summary: the car drives nicely but sadly it does not meet our needs. the boot is smaller than we thought, and…

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

signals.summary: from a mechanical standpoint the car is excellent, in line with what i've come to expect from my previous seven…
signals.quote:
from a mechanical standpoint the car is excellent, in line with what i've come to expect from my previous seven bmws. it drives smooth, is very quiet and feels luxurious.
all of the problems i've run into are tied to the software.

route planning -
there is room to improve the in-car navigation system.
1-you are unable to plan a charging route starting from anywhere other than where the vehicle is currently parked, and you cannot set a starting charge level different from the present state of charge. that makes it impossible to pre-plan the second leg of a longer trip. this information should be something you can input.
2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.
4-route planning on bmwusa.com is basically useless. try it. choose range and route, i7 e50 20", put in a starting point like 210 harbor view rd, seaview beach fl and a destination like lakeside toyota of fairview. the result is just a line on the map with state names. no city labels. no identified charging stops. nothing that actually helps an ev driver. on a previous attempt it also showed a "?" button that, when pressed, only told me i would need to charge somewhere on the way. that is not helpful.
5-i ended up having to build a spreadsheet and use my own numbers to plan the journey. i've asked the local "genius" for guidance, but the way bmw's supporting software is designed is beyond what she can assist with.
6-i'm still hoping the mistakes are mine and that you can show me a better way to use these tools. but as i see things right now, the limitations of bmw's route planing tools aren't just unhelpful - they feel insulting. maybe that would be borderline acceptable in an economy car, but not in the i7.

seat positioning -
most of the time, after i unlock, get in, start the car and buckle up, the driver's seat moves correctly from the comfort access spot to the stored position 1 for driving. however, roughly 20% of the time it doesn't move at all. and once it even slid further back instead. usually tapping the "1" button will fix it, but sometimes that button has to be held down, and sometimes only the seat controls on the door will get it to move. i suspect there might be some link to how and when i clear the nuisance disclaimer message.

updates -
not long ago i was away for about a week. the first time i drove the car after coming back, i found a lot of things had been reset. my seat memories had vanished. the custom wake word i'd set was no longer active. saying "hey bmw" did nothing, even though those options still showed as selected in the menus. there were also new displays in the instrument cluster when driving with assist plus.
it would help if:
1 - existing user settings were kept intact when an update is installed.
2-a simple message popped up at startup letting the driver know the vehicle might behave differently than it did on the last drive.

thank you for looking at my comments on this car. it's unfortunate that these frustrations exist. out of all the bmws i've owned, this is the one i am most eager to drive.

i would really like to get a response to the issues i've mentioned.

mark ellis
[EMAIL]

signals.summary: my i7 has been an absolutely fantastic car so far, and the way it drives has felt perfect to me.…
signals.quote:
my i7 has been an absolutely fantastic car so far, and the way it drives has felt perfect to me. it is extremely comfortable, and the overall quietness of the drivetrain and cabin is beyond what i have experienced with similar cars i owned before. the tech and amenities in the i7 meet or even surpass what i expect in this class. everyone who has ridden with me has been impressed with these same things. the range does drop in the winter, but for my daily use i find the range acceptable.

my only real issue with this particular car is that it arrived with bubbles in the sunroof glass, and the dealer is currently working on it. the car has been diagnosed with a manufacturer defect in the sunroof, with several small bubbles trapped between the glass layers of the panel. i am worried these imperfections could weaken the sunroof and affect safety over time, especially with temperature changes or impacts from rough or uneven roads. the team at bmw of Fairview has been great throughout all of this, showing professionalism, being transparent, and keeping me thoroughly informed while they resolve it. the problem, however, means the car needs a major teardown and repair, including removing the interior headliner, the pillar trim, the sun shade cassette, the windshield, and the driver assistance camera assembly, etc. since i have only had the car a few months, it is extremely frustrating to deal with such a big problem so early in ownership. i have barely had time to really enjoy what was supposed to be a flagship, brand-new vehicle before finding out it has to be significantly dismantled to fix this. as a long-time bmw fan and repeat owner, i have always respected the brand for its quality, precision, and innovation.

to date, the i7 has genuinely been a joy to own. in every other way it has met and even exceeded what i expect from a flagship executive sedan. the level of craftsmanship, the outstanding comfort, and the excellent noise isolation make each trip calm and very refined, which is exactly what i associate with bmw and the idea of the "ultimate driving machine." that makes this problem even more disheartening, since i expected years of worry-free enjoyment and trust in the car. with such a quiet cabin and electric drivetrain, i now fear that an invasive repair like this might never bring the car fully back to its original, factory-perfect state, and could introduce new shakes or rattles later.

Customer stated that from the time he took delivery, roughly 70% of the times he starts the vehicle the eSIM icon in the iDrive menu bar shows that the Personal eSIM is not configured and not working. Customer stated that when this occurs he cannot stream anything to the Theater Screen in the rear. Customer stated that in these instances, the iDrive Tel > Mobile devices list has the Personal eSIM entry highlighted with the note "Setting up personal eSIM" beneath it, and it never progresses or finishes. Customer stated he has gone to the dealership Genius multiple times and that the Genius adjusts something in the myBMW app to get it working again. Customer stated the fix does not last and the eSIM soon goes back to not functioning. Customer stated that he has been able to connect the eSIM and stream to the Theater Screen on some occasions, but that most of the time it fails because the eSIM never fully completes setup and connection.

Writer checked AIR and confirmed vehicle integration level G070-23-03-553 is newer than the -540 level specified for AT&T Personal eSIM. Writer connected via RVG and verified the issue: the sim card symbol with an exclamation mark in the menu bar indicated an eSIM fault. Writer confirmed the customer's description that the Tel > Mobile devices screen shows Personal eSIM highlighted with "Setting up personal eSIM" that does not change. Writer confirmed the customer was signed into his BMW ID / driver profile. Customer verified in the myBMW app that the Personal eSIM was activated on AT&T and stated he has an unlimited plan for the eSIM. Writer verified the customer's iPhone 14 is on iOS 16.5.1 and that the myBMW app is current and operating correctly.

Writer guided the customer to iDrive Menu > Vehicle apps > System settings > Update apps and services. Customer selected Update apps and services, and iDrive reported the vehicle software is current. Writer then walked the customer through a 30-second iDrive reset. Writer had the customer use the myBMW app to deactivate the eSIM from the i7. Writer next directed the customer in iDrive to Menu > Apps > Personal Hotspot > Connect new device. When the QR code appeared on the Control Display, customer stated the dealership Genius had previously skipped this step and done something different in the myBMW app, though the customer could not remember the details. Writer instructed the customer to scan the QR code. Customer stated the QR code did not proceed to move his phone further through the setup flow.

Writer then advised the customer to re-activate the eSIM using the Personal eSIM section in the myBMW app. Customer entered his phone number but the process stopped, and the app indicated he needed to add service. Writer guided the customer to select the eSIM device in iDrive and choose Activate internet access. Customer followed this, and his phone was forwarded to the AT&T login page. Customer signed into his AT&T account and tried to re-activate the eSIM on the i7, then ended the RVG session. Customer reported that on the AT&T site he was being asked to add service and that he could not re-activate the eSIM this way.

Writer explained that the problem appeared to be related to the customer's AT&T account, since AT&T was requiring added service for eSIM activation. Writer recommended that the customer contact AT&T to confirm his account and eSIM plan are truly unlimited and compatible with the Personal eSIM. Customer insisted the fault was with BMW. Writer still advised the customer to perform a 70-second iDrive hard reset to restart the telematics unit, even though the symptoms pointed more toward an AT&T account issue than telematics. Writer also recommended the customer return to the dealership so the Genius could repeat the same method they had used before to start the eSIM without involving the QR code or AT&T portal. Writer encouraged the customer to ask the dealership service department to check for any possible hardware defects due to the repeated nature of the problem. Customer did not specify what he intended to do next. Writer advised that the customer could reach out again with further questions or updates, but that the immediate next steps lay with AT&T or the dealership. Customer acknowledged.

cases.title: Frequent functions take too many steps since physical shortcuts were removed

cases.bodyMd:
## Problem

Since the move to the Curved Display with OS 8.5, owners must go through menus for functions they use many times a day (radio presets, climate, recent calls). Several owners explicitly say the **predecessor's programmable 1–8 buttons** were faster.

## Who is affected

Mostly US owners (90% of G60 verbatims are US), ICE and BEV alike. The same pattern appears in the **1 Series** (touch screen operation, 83 'difficult to use') and the **7 Series** (operating concept 33 DTU).

## Evidence summary

- Explicit wishes for physical memory and preset buttons (e.g. G60-1430, G60-1716)
- US study *menu structure* top-2 only 36%, *operation of heater/AC controls* 29%
- Web: owner threads and pro reviews call the menus 'distracting'; a broad industry move back to physical controls

## Today's car

OS 8.5 with BMW Controller; no physical favourite buttons in the option list.

## Competitors

VW and Hyundai are reintroducing physical shortcuts; Mercedes keeps a touch-heavy MBUX; Tesla is touch-only.

## Brand fit

High: eyes-on-road operation supports the 'driving dynamics' promise. AI proposal 0.85, confirmed by Lena.

## Options considered

1. Programmable physical favourite buttons (6 or 8)
2. Customisable steering-wheel shortcut
3. Software-only: 'favourites' widget pinned to the home screen (OTA)

## Decision log

- 2026-10-02 · Lena moved the case to *Investigating*
- 2026-10-09 · Engineering answered the package question → *Ready to decide*

- Explicit wishes for physical memory and preset buttons (e.g. G60-1430, G60-1716)
- US study *menu structure* top-2 only 36%, *operation of heater/AC controls* 29%
- Web: owner threads and pro reviews call the menus 'distracting'; a broad industry move back to physical controls

## Today's car

OS 8.5 with BMW Controller; no physical favourite buttons in the option list.

## Competitors

VW and Hyundai are reintroducing physical shortcuts; Mercedes keeps a touch-heavy MBUX; Tesla is touch-only.

## Brand fit

High: eyes-on-road operation supports the 'driving dynamics' promise. AI proposal 0.85, confirmed by Lena.

## Options considered

1. Programmable physical favourite buttons (6 or 8)
2. Customisable steering-wheel shortcut
3. Software-only: 'favourites' widget pinned to the home screen (OTA)

> Engineering (08.10.): 8 buttons fit the current centre stack; 6 if haptic feedback is added.

messages.content: Why is this case ranked so high?

Three factors drive the score:

1. **Regression (1.0):** owners lost something the predecessor had, the programmable 1–8 buttons [G60-1430].

3. **Brand fit (0.85, confirmed by you):** eyes-on-road operation supports driving dynamics.

The US study backs it: *menu structure* top-2 only 36%. Caveat: 90% of the verbatims are from the US, so Europe rests on the study plus one review.
Compare our planned range with the Chinese benchmarks.

On sale today: **Xiaomi SU7 Max 800 km CLTC** (trust B) [SIG-CASE-G60-CN-0003-W0]. Announced: NIO's next ET7 targets **850 km CLTC** (trust E, treat as an assumption) [SIG-CASE-G60-CN-0003-W1]. Your draft target of 750 km would sit below the on-sale benchmark. Note that the i5's published figures are **WLTP** (513–627 km); I don't mix cycles.
